messages.subject: GGIR Part 2 error subscript out of bounds
messages.subject_clean: GGIR Part 2 error subscript out of bounds
messages.body_plain:
Hi I am attempting to analyze 7 days of ActiGraph GT9x data in GGIR using the attached code. I want to examine total inactivity time for each of my participants over the 7 days and need the summary for Part 5 to do this. I have tried more than once to run this analysis and it stops running after Part 2, giving me an error in Part 5 saying: subscript out of bounds. Could this error be related to the data files themselves or the code? How can I fix the problem and get outputs for Parts 2, 4, and 5?

I do get a summary output for Part 2, which is useful for my study, but I need Parts 4 and 5 as well. I am using the most up-to-date version of GGIR. Thanks in advance for suggestions on how to correct this issue.

Jenny

Hi Raymond,

Note that GGIR allows you to specify epoch length with argument windowsizes.

The comparison you propose is not comparison between ActiLife and GGIR, but a comparison between ActiLife and the specific threshold proposed by Hildebrand and not GGIR as software tool that facilitates much more than just the Hildebrand threshold.

Thanks,

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Save data from the first and last day
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Save data from the first and last day
messages.body_plain:
Hi Zhang,

If the first or last day does not have at least 23 hours of data in the MM window analysis, it will be excluded. This is intentional. Motivation: including incomplete days will distort the time-use variable average across days.

Imagine calculating time spent in inactivity (sedentary behaviour if you like) for a person who consistently does it  for 14 hours per day each day of the year. For the first and last recording day you may miss half of the day, by which you would only capture 7 of those 14 hours. If you include those incomplete days the final average across all the days you would get ((7 x 2) + (14 x 5)) / 7 = 12 hours, which is not correct because the true behaviour of the person is 14 hours per day.

This is why time-use analysis should always rely on complete days with a low amount of non-wear or have a clever way of imputing the missing hours using imputed behavioural patterns. GGIR currently does not have that, and I am not sure it even exists yet. If this would be added, we could be more flexible with the inclusion of days.

Another solution is to collect more recording days.

For waking-up to waking-up (WW) window analyses in part 5, the first or last day may additionally be excluded because no reliable estimate can be made of waking-up time to define the edge of those days.

Best,

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Looking for an explanation of MVPA parameters.
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Looking for an explanation of MVPA parameters.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jan,

> How does GGIR calculate the MVPA (bouts, min. percentage of time reached certain values).

See code and documentation for GGIR function g.getbout,  as this is where the bouts are detected.

> Specificly I'm interested in the  -dur_day_total_MOD_min -dur_day_total_VIG_min
I think it's 1 min bouts with maybe a minimum of 80% of the time reached 100 mg's. Could that be right?

These two output variables are time spent in acceleration ranges, and do not reflect time spent in bouts. See: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#43_Output_part_5

Dr. Vincent van Hees

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jenny,

Your g.shell.GGIR script looks normal to me, I do not see anything suspicious. So, I think the best option is to step by step investigate where the problem may originate:
- Does part 2 output indicate that there is data for most of the 7 days and that the accelerometers were worn (valid hours data), and does the QC plot generated by part 2 look positive with no yellow (invalid data) during the nights?
- For part 3: Are RData files generated in meta/ms3.out folder?
- For part 4: Are RData files generated in meta/ms4.out folder? If yes, are you getting the part 4 csv report in the results folder? If yes, do estimates look plausible.
- For part 5: Are RData files generated in meta/ms5.out folder?

What can also help is starting in a new input and output folder and trying to only process a single file.

Good luck!
Vincent

messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] GGIR Part 2 error subscript out of bounds
messages.body_plain:
Sounds good. Other things you could try:
- Check that the QC folder has a part4 .csv report. If yes, then the cleaningcode column in that files may clarify why no sleep report was created in the results folder. Cleaningcodes are clarified in the GGIR vignette <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html>.
- Rerun part 3 (mode=3, overwrite=TRUE) but now with do.part3.pdf=TRUE, which should create a sleep.qc folder inside the meta-folder, and then store in it pdf files with plots of time series data. These plots corresponding to the various days. Time lines reflect acceleration (grey), arm angle (black), sleep classification (red), light if collected (yellow) and temperature if collected (blue).

Vincent

messages.subject_clean: GGIR seems to ignore Timestamps while performing analysis on actigraph data
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
while analysis of accelerometric data is not my main field of research, colleagues asked me for help analyzing data of 2500 participants and they wanted to use the GGIR R-package. I did some testings with data from a smaller study and everything worked fine. Now I just got some real data from the bigger cohort study and they had the Idle Sleep Mode for the Actigraph device activated. As a result we got Raw data csv files with different lengths and leaps in time between them. Is there any way to take this into account using GGIR? At the moment it seems like R is ignoring the timestamps and uses just the 3 movement axis. I added the QC pdf to illustrate the problem. I hope anyone can help us to solve this problem.

Best regards

Dominic Bläsing

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Issue with meta/ms3.out/NA folder
messages.body_plain:
Two possible issues:

f0=0
You probably need to change this ot f0=1. Note that in GGIR, and more generally in R, we count from one up as opposed to zero, common in some other programming environments.  So, first file is indexed with 1.

mode = c(1,2,5)
This would only work if mode =c(1,2, 3,4) has been run previously and the milestone data generated from that is still in the output folder. GGIR needs to run it's part 3 and 4, in order to be able to do part 5.

I hope this helps.
Cheers, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR seems to be unable to classify multiple sleep periods on one day.
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] GGIR seems to be unable to classify multiple sleep periods on one day.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Romy,

You may want to have a look at the .csv-reports first, because those are core results, which have been tested extensively in datasets with irregular sleep patterns.

The pdf visualisation is an attempt to visualise the quantitative results, but especially when sleep is irregular the timing of sleep window isn't always shown correctly, which is something that needs improving. For the time being it is probably good to treat the timing of sleep in the pdf visualisation with caution.

GGIR tries to detect the largest sleep period in the day. I know this doesn't fit well with the scenario where people have irregular sleep and end up with multiple main sleep periods in the day. However, note that the day time 'sustained inactivity bouts (=sib)'  are reported in the GGIR part 4 csv-report. I am trying to be careful with calling them naps as whether they are naps needs more research. You can use these to get a sense of overall time spend in behaviours that look like sleep/resting by adding up sleep in the sleep period time window (nocturnal sleep) and daytime resting (=those sib periods).

Vincent
